description: Shallow, flat-bottomed pan with sloped sides and a long handle, for frying and searing.
Wide pan with straight or high sides and usually a lid, for frying, braising and reducing.
Sealed pot that cooks under steam pressure; stovetop and electric versions exist.
Container made to the gastronorm size standard, used in commercial kitchens and serving counters.
Grill that cooks food over a fire, charcoal, gas or electric heat.
Appliance that cooks rice in an inner pot under automatic control. Heating type ranges from conventional to micom, induction and pressure induction.
Heated water bath that keeps food warm or cooks it gently, used in commercial kitchens.
Set of pots and pans of one maker line, sold and rated as one product.
Mid-size kitchen knife between the paring knife and the chef's knife (not the workshop utility knife, which is in Tools & Workshop Equipment).
Thick, single-bevel Japanese knife for butchering fish.
Long, single-bevel Japanese knife for slicing raw fish.
Thin, single-bevel Japanese vegetable knife with a straight edge.
Hand mill that grinds pepper or spices. A grinder for coffee is under Coffee, tea & water.
Scale for weighing ingredients; some connect to an app.
Insulated, powered cabinet that keeps food and drink cold; built-in or freestanding.
Insulated bag for carrying a meal and keeping it cool.
Reusable bottle for carrying a drink, sport or not.
Flexible drink reservoir with a drinking tube, sold on its own.
Large flat plate on which a main meal is served and eaten; a commemorative or display plate is also listed here.
Fork laid at the place setting for eating.
Spoon laid at the place setting for eating.
Knife laid at the place setting for eating.
Sharp, often serrated table knife for cutting meat at the plate.
Blunt table knife for spreading butter.
Handled cup for tea or coffee, usually used with a saucer; a cup and saucer sold together is listed here.
Tray made to carry and serve food and drink.
Rigid mat set under a place setting; a textile placemat is in Soft Furnishings.
Small hard mat set under a glass or cup.
Burr or blade grinder made for coffee beans, by hand or electric.
Lidded vessel with a spout and handle for brewing and pouring tea; Yixing teapots are included.
Japanese teapot with a side handle.
Lidded bowl on a saucer for brewing tea.
Vessel that boils water, on the stove or electric; the Japanese iron tetsubin is included.
Jug with a filter cartridge that treats water for drinking; replacement cartridges are in Climate, Water & Energy.
Rack on which washed dishes stand to drain and dry.
Long-handled spoon for stirring and serving in cooking, solid or slotted. Spoons for eating are under Tableware & serveware.
